subject: StratusIQ: competitive inference recap and proposed next tests
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Erik Johnson <erik@stratusiq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: StratusIQ: competitive inference recap and proposed next tests

Hi Erik —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and so we can land concrete next steps: 

Summary of what we heard from StratusIQ
- You are running a bakeoff across Redwood + two hyperscaler inference APIs (CloudFast and MegaServe).
- Primary evaluation axes: hallucination rate on your domain prompts, throughput/latency at 1–5k QPS, and per-token cost at expected batch sizes.
- Procurement has asked for latency SLO targets and SOC2 evidence before procurement conversation.

Immediate findings (from your side-by-side):
- The hyperscaler endpoints were cheaper at high batch sizes but showed higher hallucination rates on your rare-entity prompts (examples attached).
- Prefix caching helped latency materially on our side; we think KV cache/continuous batching is a differentiator for latency-sensitive paths.

Proposed next tests (high level) — we’ll own the infra/workbook:
1) Prompt battery: we attached a first-pass CSV (stratus_prompt_battery.csv) with 150 prompts — split by intent, entity density, and adversarial phrasing.
2) Deterministic hallucination metric: define a per-response hallucination score and run comparatives across the three endpoints at 1, 5, 25 token samples.
3) Regression checks: a small baseline of golden prompts to run before/after model or infra changes.
4) Cost/latency sweep: test at batch sizes [1,8,32] with KV cache on/off.

Asks from us to you
- Can you share the internal procurement SLO template (latency/cost targets)?
- Are you able to run the CSV locally in your sandbox, or should we spin up a quick sandbox account and run the tests?

I’ve cc'd Ben (sales eng) and Jasmine (research) — Ben and Jas, can you propose an initial runbook and a concrete A/B matrix by EOD tomorrow? I’ll coordinate scheduling with Erik afterwards.

Attachments: stratus_prompt_battery.csv (sample prompts)

Next meeting options: Mon 10/18 10:00–10:30 PT or Tue 10/19 14:00–14:30 PT — which works for you, Erik?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Erik Johnson <erik@stratusiq.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StratusIQ: competitive inference recap and proposed next tests

Thanks — wrote up a starter matrix and a few concrete eval prompts so we can move quickly. Attached: runbook-initial.md (high-level steps and owner map).

Quick test matrix (will expand in runbook):
- Runs: Redwood, CloudFast, MegaServe
- Payloads: 150 prompt battery (split as attached), plus 20 golden regression prompts (sensitive entity cases)
- Configs: batch sizes [1,8,32], KV cache [on, off], temperature [0.0, 0.7]
- Metrics: hallucination_rate (see definition below), average latency p50/p95/p99, cost_per_1M_tokens, semantic-similarity-F1 (auto + human spot checks)

Hallucination_rate (proposal): fraction of generated responses that assert an ungrounded fact relative to the prompt's context. Annotator instructions + an automated classifier for quick sweep; each failure triggers human triage on a 10% sample.

Example evaluation prompts to include in the battery (short form):
1) "Given the following customer record, write a summary and highlight any inferred relationships." (entity-heavy)
2) "Does product X support encryption at rest for archived snapshots? If so, cite the exact policy text." (requires precise policy recall)
3) "User asks: 'Which of our accounts have had >3 failed logins this month?' Provide a concise list and suggested remediation." (requires extraction and non-hallucination)

Action owners (first pass):
- Ben: implement runner and baseline Redwood vs hyperscalers, provide raw metrics and CSV by EOD Mon 10/18
- Jasmine: build annotation guideline and run initial automated hallucination classifier; hand off human sample backlog to the Stratus security contact for review
- Monica: coordinate procurement SLO template and follow up on sandbox access

Attachments: runbook-initial.md

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
